title: The Lunenburg Budget Project — FY28 and beyond
Budget Crisis
points: Projections show a $930k deficit next year, and one in every year after it. | The budget in force already cut 9.2 FTE, and the projection reopens anyway. | Costs grow 5.18% a year and revenue 3.03%: a rate problem, not a bad year. | Salaries and health insurance are 64% of the budget — the only two lines that can change the direction, and neither is a School Committee vote. | About $795k a year of free cash could go to the schools, and it is one-time money.
point_1: Projections show a $930k deficit next year, and one in every year after it.
point_2: The budget in force already cut 9.2 FTE, and the projection reopens anyway.
point_3: Costs grow 5.18% a year and revenue 3.03%: a rate problem, not a bad year.
point_4: Salaries and health insurance are 64% of the budget — the only two lines that can change the direction, and neither is a School Committee vote.
point_5: About $795k a year of free cash could go to the schools, and it is one-time money.

title: Straight answers
points: $930k — The schools need $930,273 more next year than the town can give them. That is the whole problem, in one number. | 2.68% — The things schools buy get 5.18% more expensive each year. State law lets the town collect about 2.5% more each year. Nobody overspent — the two numbers are simply different. | $570k — That difference opens a brand new hole every year, of roughly $570,339 to $786,364, whether or not you closed the last one. | 1 yr — So no single cut fixes this. title: The situation
points: Cutting every extra still funded — $376,207 — covers 40% of next year’s gap, once. | ~90% — Contracts, insurance and law set about 90% of the budget; after the extras, only classroom positions are big enough to cut. | 2.25 pts — The published cost increase is 3.98%; the one that comes back every year is 6.23%.
point_1: Cutting every extra still funded — $376,207 — covers 40% of next year’s gap, once.
point_2: ~90% — Contracts, insurance and law set about 90% of the budget; after the extras, only classroom positions are big enough to cut.
point_3: 2.25 pts — The published cost increase is 3.98%; the one that comes back every year is 6.23%.

title: Free cash — how much is actually spendable
points: 47% — Free cash is not money the town saved. point_1: 47% — Free cash is not money the town saved. It is mostly money the town budgeted and did not spend.

title: The money outside the budget
points: The town’s funds outside the budget took in more than they spent in 12 of 13 years, and what they hold multiplied 3.6×. | 34% of what those funds hold is pandemic-era money, and this series ends before we can see whether it has gone. | Most of the money held outside the budget is not school money — a large part is water, sewer and trash. | FY23 was the first year since FY17 that the school funds spent more than they took in.
